title: Global minimization of Hölder-smooth convex functions: a public quadratic regularizer; exact gradients
summary: Find an approximate global minimizer, with accuracy measured by suboptimality of the complete objective.

description_paragraphs: Find an approximate global minimizer, with accuracy measured by suboptimality of the complete objective.
$$\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}F(x)$$
The complete objective is $F(x)=h(x)+\frac\mu2\|x-x_0\|_2^2$, with a public quadratic regularizer.

$F(x)=h(x)+\mu\|x-x_0\|_2^2/2$, where $h$ is globally convex and has a $
u$-Hölder continuous Euclidean gradient, with $0<
u<1$. Assume $F(x_0)-F^\star\le\Delta$. Gradient access to the unknown function $h$ is equivalent to gradient access to $F$. The complete objective $F$ need not have a globally $
u$-Hölder continuous gradient.

Admissible parameter domain:

$$ eta_
u>0,\quad d\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1},\quad \varepsilon>0,\quad 
u>0,\quad 
u\le1,\quad \Delta>0,\quad \mu>0,\quad 
u<1$$

proofs.title: Public regularization of Hölder-smooth objectives
proofs.body:
Let $F=h+\mu\|x-x_0\|^2/2$, with unknown convex $h$ whose global gradient is $
u$-Hölder, $0<
u<1$. At error scale $u$, strong convexity provides radius $O(\sqrt{u/\mu})$. The cited Hölder accelerated bound reduces error by a constant factor in
$$
C_
u[ eta_
u^2/(\mu^{1+
u}u^{1-
u})]^{1/(1+3
u)}
$$
calls, plus constant initialization. Restarting over geometric scales gives the final-stage power term plus $O(\log(2+\Delta/\epsilon))$. The public quadratic changes no oracle count.

For the randomized lower bound, scale the cited global Hölder hard family to minimizer radius $r=c\sqrt{\epsilon/\mu}$. An $\epsilon$-solution of $F$ is a $2\epsilon$-solution of $h$: compare with that minimizer, whose added quadratic is $O(\epsilon)$. One response still uses one $h$ query. Substituting $r$ gives
$$
c_
u[ eta_
u^2/(\mu^{1+
u}\epsilon^{1-
u})]^{1/(1+3
u)}.
$$
Retain the initial-gap requirement
$\Delta\ge C_
u eta_
u(\epsilon/\mu)^{(1+
u)/2}$
and the original sufficient dimension. The random lower bound uses the globally shielded construction; a deterministic resisting oracle is not a substitute. Constants may depend on fixed $
u$.
proofs.scope: Global Hölder regularity of the unknown convex term; known quadratic regularization.
proofs.limitations: Fixed exponent, initial-gap admissibility, and sufficient dimension are retained. The total objective is not globally Hölder of exponent less than one.
